chunks: (And) they would hasten forward, heads lifted upwards, gazes fixed, and emptied out their hearts.

key_terms.أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ: Their hearts (plural of fad'ah, referring to the core of the heart)
key_terms.مُهْطِعِينَ: Hastening forward with speed and urgency

ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual characteristics of people on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ibrahim vividly depicts the psychological and spiritual collapse of the disbelievers, where their frantic haste (muhtadiheen) contrasts with their paralyzed awe. The metaphor of hearts being 'hollow air' (hawa') signifies a complete void of divine insight and reason, leaving them devoid of any capacity to comprehend the truth they once rejected.
